title: Keyboard Manager doesn't work properly through remote desktop

status.label: Reproduce remapping across RDP
status.detail: Exact Esc/Caps Lock steps already exist; local suppression, remote toggle state and double remapping need separation.

next_action.label: Run host/remote remapping matrix
next_action.reason: Do not request the supplied steps again or assume every remote symptom has one cause.

judgment.rationale: The body gives a deterministic Esc/Caps Lock swap and mstsc sequence. Later reports add Ctrl/Caps Lock and a separate double-remapping case; disabling host-side remapping resolved that case, not necessarily the original.
evidence: PowerToys 0.63.0 reports the remote session receiving both Caps Lock behavior and remapped Esc.
All six comments were read, including the host-plus-remote remapping workaround and excluded-app request.
KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp constructs remapped INPUT events, handles Caps Lock/modifier edge cases and suppresses handled originals; Input.h wraps SendInput.
Duplicate cross-references and open related CloudPC issue 32879 supply context but no targeted merged fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with Keyboard Manager enabled host-only, remote-only and both; trace original/injected transitions before choosing a transport-compatible correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: A bounded input-path investigation is applicable; the current discussion does not establish a specific implementation or a universal workaround.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve remapped key and toggle semantics across Remote Desktop
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed: local virtual-key injection and Caps Lock toggle synchronization may be represented differently through RDP. Running the same remap at both endpoints is a separate possible double-remapping cause.
plan: Establish the original Esc/Caps Lock failure on a current build and a clean mstsc session with remapping on only one endpoint.
Trace local low-level-hook input, injected keydown/up and remote received key/toggle state; compare host-only, remote-only and both-endpoint configurations.
If the injected representation or Caps Lock synchronization is confirmed responsible, correct that narrow translation while retaining original-event suppression and balanced modifier releases.
Keep application exclusion as a separate product decision; do not bypass all remaps or inject an extra original key as a speculative fix.
Add regressions for Caps Lock/Esc, Caps Lock/Ctrl, ordinary non-toggle remaps, disconnected/reconnected sessions and local apps.
verification: Remote Esc presses produce one Escape action and no unintended Caps Lock transition.
Remote Caps Lock follows the configured mapping without stuck Ctrl/Shift/Alt states.
Local remaps and failed-injection passthrough remain functional.

confidence.rationale: The public reproduction is concrete and source confirms injection/suppression boundaries, but no input trace establishes whether transport translation, toggle synchronization or double remapping explains the original.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager remapping can leak Caps Lock behavior through Remote Desktop; later comments include both matching symptoms and a distinct double-remapping configuration.
known_information: The original report supplies a numbered Esc/Caps Lock reproduction.
A commenter resolved their host-plus-remote configuration by disabling host Keyboard Manager.
The source already has Caps Lock handling, original-event suppression and failed-injection passthrough.
inferences: RDP/toggle synchronization is a plausible boundary to investigate, not a proven missing-suppression defect.
issue_context.analysis: A generic request for steps and a diagnostic ZIP would ignore the existing deterministic scenario. Maintainer instrumentation is more useful for separating the endpoint configurations.
initial_investigation: Read the full report, all six comments and linked-work timeline.
Inspected KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp and the common SendVirtualInput wrapper.
Distinguished the existing double-remapping workaround from the original host-only behavior.

actions.label: Review remote-input investigation plan
actions.description: Approve the bounded hypothesis-testing plan before any input translation change.

prerequisites: Use two Windows endpoints with mstsc access and record Windows/PowerToys versions.
Prepare an instrumented Keyboard Manager build and a remote key-event/toggle-state observer; record existing mappings before changing them.
steps: Swap Esc and Caps Lock on the host only; connect with mstsc and press/release each key.
Repeat windowed and full-screen while recording local injected events and remote keydown/up/toggle state.
Disable host remaps and enable the mapping only remotely; repeat.
Enable the mapping on both endpoints as a separate double-remap control; repeat with Caps Lock/Ctrl and an ordinary key.
reproduce.expected_result: Exactly the configured remote key action occurs with balanced transitions and no unexpected Caps Lock toggle.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare a two-endpoint RDP test with event capture on both sides. Keep host-only, remote-only and both-endpoint Keyboard Manager cases separate, and avoid recording unrelated typed content.
